messages.subject: scale_x_discrete : drop argument
parts:
Hi,

I'm running R v 2.9.2 and ggplot2 v 0.8.3

d <- data.frame(x=c("a", "b", "c"), y=1:3)

qplot(x, y, data=d[1:2,]) + scale_x_discrete(drop=FALSE)
qplot(x, y, data=d[1:2,]) + scale_x_discrete(drop=TRUE)

On my computer, the two graphs are identical (and include "c" on the
axis). Is that reproducible? If yes, is it a bug or is it me not
understanding what "drop" should do?

Thanks,

Xavier

messages.subject: Re: scale_x_discrete : drop argument
parts:
On Thu, Oct 8, 2009 at 10:55 AM, Xavier <cha...@agroparistech.fr> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I'm running R v 2.9.2 and ggplot2 v 0.8.3
>
> d <- data.frame(x=c("a", "b", "c"), y=1:3)
>
> qplot(x, y, data=d[1:2,]) + scale_x_discrete(drop=FALSE)
> qplot(x, y, data=d[1:2,]) + scale_x_discrete(drop=TRUE)
>
> On my computer, the two graphs are identical (and include "c" on the
> axis). Is that reproducible? If yes, is it a bug or is it me not
> understanding what "drop" should do?

I think this is a bug, but I'm not sure how to fix it. The problem is
that there's a semi-complicated interaction with facetting - if scales
are fixed, then you can only drop levels that don't appear in any of
the facets, and if scales are free and you have categorical variables
then you expect extra levels within a facet to be dropped without
having to also say scale_x_discrete(drop = TRUE).

Maybe I should change the default to drop = TRUE and not override your
choice when scales = "free" as I'm currently doing. The potential
problem with this is that if you are facetting with scales = "fixed"
and some levels don't appear on every facet, then there's a
possibility the factors will get rearranged.

So maybe a better solution would be to drop levels automatically
whenever drop = T OR when scales = "free".

Ok - I've tried this out and it seems to work ok, so it will be fixed
in the next version.
